intro: Togo is a narrow West African country that was a German colony, then French, and has been led by one family since 1967.

chapters.title: Early peoples
text: Ewe, Kabye and other peoples lived here before Europeans arrived. The Batammariba built tall mud tower-houses in Koutammakou, now a World Heritage site.

chapters.title: German and French Togo
text: Germany made Togoland a colony in 1884. After World War One it was split between Britain and France; the British part later joined Ghana. French Togo became independent in 1960.

chapters.title: The Gnassingbé era
text: Gnassingbé Eyadéma took power in 1967 and ruled until his death in 2005. His son Faure Gnassingbé succeeded him. A 2024 constitution moved power to a new post of President of the Council of Ministers, which Faure took in 2025.

timeline.title: Occupation
timeline.text: British and French troops take Togoland.

keyTerms.meaning: The German colony that included Togo.
